displayedInputs.question: Calculate \((1+i)(1-i)\).
Calculate \(i^2\).
Calculate \(i^4\).
What is the real part of \((2+i)(1+0i)\)?
What is the real part of \((4+6i)/2\)?
What is the imaginary part of \((4+6i)/2\)?
The conjugate of \(1+i\) is \(1-i\). What is their product?
What does \((1+i)/(1+i)\) equal?
\(i^3=-i\). What is its imaginary part?
Calculate \((1+2i)(1-2i)\).
Calculate \((3+i)(3-i)\).
Which cycle do the positive integer powers of \(i\) follow, starting from \(i^1\)?
The base radius of a cylinder and the base radius of a cone are the same, both being 3. What is this common radius?
When finding the volume of a composite solid, what is the usual approach?

choices.A: Always use a single formula to calculate it in one step
choices.C: Divide it into several basic solids, then add or subtract their volumes

displayedInputs.question: In a figure placed horizontally, a line segment parallel to the horizontal axis has length 6. What length should this segment have in the pictorial drawing?
A line segment parallel to the vertical axis has length 8. What length should it have in an oblique dimetric drawing?
A line segment parallel to the vertical axis in the original figure has length 3 in the pictorial drawing. What was its original length?
In an oblique dimetric drawing, what angle is usually drawn between the horizontal and vertical axes?
A square with side length 4 is placed in a horizontal plane, with one side parallel to the horizontal axis. What is the length of this side in the pictorial drawing?
What is the length in the pictorial drawing of another side of this square perpendicular to that side?
In an oblique dimetric drawing, line segments that were originally parallel:
Two line segments, both parallel to the horizontal axis in the pictorial drawing, originally had lengths 5 and 5. What is the sum of their lengths in the pictorial drawing?
In the volume formula for a sphere, what power of the radius is used?
How many planes are determined by three points that do not lie on the same line?
If two distinct planes have a common point, then which statement holds?

choices.A: They have only this one common point
choices.D: They have one and only one common line through that point

displayedInputs.question: What is determined by a line and a point outside the line?
What are skew lines?

choices.A: Lines that intersect but are not perpendicular
choices.C: Lines that lie in the same plane but do not intersect
choices.D: Two lines that do not lie in any common plane

displayedInputs.question: How many intersection points do two intersecting lines in space have?
Which statement holds for parallel lines in space?

choices.C: They are coplanar and have no common points

displayedInputs.question: How many types of relative positions are there between a line and a plane?

choices.A: Three: lying in the plane, parallel, and intersecting

displayedInputs.question: What can be said about two distinct planes?
When a line intersects a plane, how many points do they have in common?
If two points on a line lie in a plane, what follows?

choices.A: The line is parallel to the plane
choices.B: The line and the plane have only one point of intersection
choices.C: The line is perpendicular to the plane
choices.D: The entire line lies in this plane

displayedInputs.question: Line \(a\) does not lie in a plane, and \(a\) is parallel to line \(b\) in the plane. What follows?
If \(a\) is parallel to \(b\) in a plane, but \(a\) itself also lies in this plane, what is the conclusion?

choices.C: We cannot say that \(a\) is parallel to the plane

displayedInputs.question: How many lines in the plane does the criterion use as a reference?
When a line is parallel to a plane, how many points do the line and the plane have in common?
Line \(a\) is parallel to plane \(\alpha\). A plane containing \(a\) intersects \(\alpha\) along \(b\). What follows?
What is the difference between a criterion theorem and a property theorem?

choices.B: A property is used to draw pictorial diagrams
choices.C: A criterion is used only for perpendicularity
choices.D: A criterion deduces parallelism from conditions, while a property deduces new parallelism from existing parallelism

displayedInputs.question: A line \(a\) is parallel to a plane \(\alpha\). A distinct plane \(\beta\) contains \(a\) and intersects \(\alpha\). How many lines form the intersection of \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\)?
